items: “How would you manage an RhD-negative pregnant woman?”

blocks.text: “I would confirm her ABO and RhD status and perform an antibody screen. If she is RhD negative and unsensitised, I would provide routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis according to local protocol and administer additional anti-D following appropriate sensitising events. I would document previous pregnancies and sensitising events carefully. If clinically significant antibodies are detected, I would identify the antibody and determine whether this represents passive prophylactic anti-D or true alloimmunisation. In established alloimmunisation, anti-D is no longer useful, and I would refer for specialist fetal surveillance, particularly MCA peak systolic velocity Doppler to assess for fetal anaemia. If significant fetal anaemia develops, fetal medicine assessment for possible intrauterine transfusion or appropriately timed delivery would be required.”
